sig domain: node-derived separation end-to-end for devnet/testnet (#32)
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/33

Implements the end-to-end signature-domain separation gated on #32, in the shape agreed there: node-derived, a separate set-once override beside `GENESIS_BLOCK_ID`, the compiled constant never mutated.

## Mechanism

- **`genesis.rs`** — `OnceLock<Hash256>` override + `bind_signature_domain(genesis_id)`: set-once, same-id rebind is an idempotent `Ok` (every pre-sign helper routes through it), different-id rebind returns `Err(bound)`. `signature_domain()` falls back to the compiled canonical id when never bound. `sig_message` (transaction.rs) reads it.
- **`rpc.rs`** — `get_block_height` now carries `genesis_block_id`, sourced from `node.genesis_id` (the P2P handshake identity, sync.rs), never tip-derived. Asserted by the contract test below.
- **`types/mod.rs`** — `enter_devnet()` composes coinbase maturity 1 AND the devnet domain bind in one auditable call. Two gated callers: `run_node`'s `if devnet` arm, and the signer path below. `node`/`mine` never bind.
- **`wallet/auth.rs`** — `ensure_signature_domain`: ONE read of the node's reported genesis id, default-deny against what the signer already holds (the compiled id, or an id named via `--expect-genesis`), then `bind` of the exact checked id — no re-fetch between check and bind (the TOCTOU from review point 2). Routed through `authenticated_output_lookup`, the pre-sign choke point every spend path already crosses — including the inline-signing `HtlcClaim`/`HtlcReclaim` arms (review point 1) — plus fail-fast calls in `fetch_utxos_select` and the wallet-send RPC arm. A node that reports no genesis id (older `get_block_height`) is accepted only under the canonical expectation, where the unbound fallback is already what that node verifies; an explicit expectation it cannot verify is an error.
- **`main.rs`** — global `--expect-genesis <GENESIS_ID|devnet>` (the `devnet` sugar resolves to `devnet_genesis_block().block_id()`, a compiled constant). No blanket accept-any flag exists. `exfer devnet` prints its genesis id and the flag hint at startup.

## Coverage: five signing surfaces, structurally

`wallet send` (`Wallet::build_transaction`), `sign_p2pkh` locks, `sign_tx_with_wallet` spends, and the two inline signers `HtlcClaim`/`HtlcReclaim` all reach `sig_message` only after `authenticated_output_lookup`/`fetch_utxos_select` has run fetch→check→bind against the node they are about to submit to. The per-subcommand test spawns the real binary for **all 20 CLI signing invocations** against a mock node reporting a foreign genesis id and asserts: nonzero exit, the trust-rule error, and that the mock saw nothing but `get_block_height` — a future subcommand that signs without routing through the shared helpers fails this suite.
